name: Solaz
positioning: Solaz, a Luxury Collection Resort, Los Cabos: a contemporary Mexican beachfront resort on the Sea of Cortez, between San José del Cabo and Cabo San Lucas, with architecture by Sordo Madaleno and a thalassotherapy spa
best_for: Design lovers drawn to contemporary Mexican architecture and art
Couples wanting rooms with plunge pools, outdoor showers and ocean views
Families who want a kids club, a teens club and multi-bedroom villa space

facts.text: Solaz sits on the coast of Baja California Sur, between San José del Cabo and Cabo San Lucas, on the Sea of Cortez.
The resort is designed in contemporary Mexican style using warm indigenous woods, and a wrapping infinity pool meets the stretch of sand.
Its stone-and-glass structures are built low into the desert terrain, with commissioned Mexican art and native landscaping.
More than 150 endemic plants are woven into the landscape to cut down on water use.
Rooms are designed with local Mexican huanacaxtle wood and marble textures, and select accommodations have private plunge pools.
The One Bedroom Ocean View Suite has a private balcony with a hammock and an outdoor hot tub.
The Wellness Suite features a bed massage table and a private steam room.
Ojo de Liebre Spa + Thalasso, inspired by Baja's Ojo de Liebre lagoon, brings together ancient wellness traditions, thalassotherapy and contemporary treatments.
Private beach and pool cabanas are available with personalized service.
Baja Beach serves Mexican Pacific cuisine and cocktails from a beachside Airstream.
The Cabo Nauta kids club has reading caves and a kid-friendly kitchen, and the 13|19 Teens Club has pool tables, foosball, video game stations and arcade basketball.
Artisan Butler Service offers a personalized approach, with bespoke itineraries and local recommendations from a dedicated Artisan.

highlights.text: The architecture is by Sordo Madaleno, with sculptures and art by César López-Negrete.
The spa has seawater and fresh water pools, 12 treatment rooms, hot and ice-cold tubs, aromatherapy, chromotherapy light showers and a cryotherapy chamber.
Villa Solaz has four bedrooms, an expansive terrace and two family pools, with a private chef and a dedicated artisan butler.
The infinity pools are designed with butterfly green granite that mirrors the turquoise waters beyond.
The Gabinete del Barco exhibit is an indigenous gallery of regional artifacts, including a suspended skeleton of a 13-meter-long grey whale.

considerations.text: Los Cabos International Airport is approximately 34.7 km from the hotel.
The minimum age to check in is 18.
WhataHotel notes premium pricing that reflects the resort's luxury positioning.
